propositions: A configured bedrock provider is silently dropped when the model id contains a colon (the canonical versioned form 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), causing the provider qualifier to be lost and a misleading error naming a model fragment instead of the actual provider

The _resolve_target and infer_provider functions independently implement the same colon-based test for provider qualification, allowing them to drift and creating two separate failure paths for the same bug
An explicitly configured provider must be honored regardless of punctuation in the model id; a conflicting configured-provider/inline-qualifier pair must raise rather than silently pick a winner
The qualified/unqualified decision must check a configured provider first (guard order) before scanning the model string, so no model-id punctuation can overrule or discard an explicit instruction

Both Bedrock id shapes (unversioned aliases like 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6' and canonical versioned like 'anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0') must resolve correctly with configured provider='bedrock'

The provider qualifier decision must be centralized in one shared function so both deciders cannot drift, and provider-name shape validation must distinguish identifier-like prefixes from model-id fragments
